name: otr-many-facts
about: An over-the-road job with many facts: enough for five angles that differ in kind. Its brief is shaped as a real opening's (`openingSubjectMatter`): the job details are the equipment and the schedule, and every benefit is a listed term.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: Family owned, and the owner still drives

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Our ads with hook equipment_first (equipment first) and scene equipment_at_rest (truck at rest) spent $402.10 in the last 28 days over 30100 impressions and brought 14 leads, $28.72 per lead.

output.audience: Experienced Class A drivers who already run over-the-road, in reefer or similar long-haul freight, and are used to long stretches out. They want a stronger pay per mile, newer equipment and freight they do not unload. Plain facts about pay, the freight and who owns the company would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the late-model truck the driver would run, parked and clean, with the reefer trailer behind it.
angles.proof: The opening offers late-model equipment and the freight is reefer.
angles.why: This hook and scene brought leads at a cost per lead under the benchmark's pause line. The lead count is modest, so treat it as a good sign, not proof.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile, shown over a truck out on the open highway.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay per mile and that the runs are over-the-road across the states it lists.
angles.why: Pay per mile is the hardest fact on the sheet, and long runs make it matter. Nothing has been measured for this hook yet.

angles.idea: Say plainly what the job asks: Class A licence, the years the opening states, the weeks it states, reefer, over-the-road.
angles.proof: The opening names the licence class, a years figure, a weeks figure and over-the-road runs.
angles.why: No lead outcomes exist yet, so stating the requirements up front is the cheapest guard against wrong-fit leads. The office should confirm what the weeks figure means before writing.

angles.idea: Lead with life in the cab: the pet rides along and the driver does not touch the freight.
angles.proof: The opening offers a pet policy and no-touch freight.
angles.why: Drivers out for long stretches weigh daily life in the truck as much as pay. Untested here, so nothing measured supports it yet.

angles.idea: Lead with who runs the company: family owned, and the owner still drives, backed by the benefits the opening lists.
angles.proof: The carrier describes itself as family owned with an owner who still drives, and the opening lists health insurance and paid time off.
angles.why: An owner who still drives is a claim that sets this carrier apart and needs no picture to land. Untested for this carrier.
